easy.def: To eat with tiny bites.
examples: The mouse will nibble the cheese.
Fish nibble at the bread.
I nibble my cracker.

more.def: To eat something by taking small bites.
examples: The rabbit nibbled on a carrot.
Mice had nibbled a hole in the bag of grain.
The goat nibbled at my sleeve.

easy.def: Kind and friendly.
examples: She is a nice girl.
He was nice to me.
What a nice dog!

more.def: Kind, friendly, or pleasant.
examples: The nice neighbor brought us a basket of apples.
We had a nice walk along the beach.
It is nice to see you again.

easy.def: In a pleasant or good way.
examples: She wrote nicely.
The cake turned out nicely.
He asked nicely.

more.def: In a good, pleasing or kind way.
examples: She wrote her name nicely.
The new couch fits nicely in the corner.
He asked nicely for a turn.

easy.def: A coin worth five cents.
examples: I have a nickel.
A nickel is five cents.
I found a nickel.

more.def: A coin that is worth five cents.
examples: I found a nickel under the couch.
Five nickels make a quarter.
The gumball cost a nickel.

easy.def: A short or funny name used by friends.
examples: My nickname is Joe.
Her nickname is Bee.
I got a nickname.

more.def: A friendly name that people use instead of your real name.
examples: My nickname is Max, short for Maxwell.
Her friends gave her the nickname Sunny.
The coach gave each player a nickname.

easy.def: The daughter of your brother or sister.
examples: She is my niece.
My niece is two.
I read to my niece.

more.def: The daughter of someone's brother or sister.
examples: My niece is learning to walk.
Aunt Jo took her niece to the zoo.
I made a card for my niece.

easy.def: Clever and very good.
examples: That is a nifty tool.
He has a nifty hat.
She made a nifty trick.

more.def: Neat, clever or very good.
examples: She showed us a nifty trick with a card.
The hiker used a nifty tool that folded up small.
That nifty gadget peels apples in seconds.

easy.def: The time when it is dark and people sleep.
examples: The moon shines at night.
Good night!
I sleep all night.

more.def: The time between sunset and sunrise, when it is dark outside.
examples: Owls hunt at night when the forest is quiet.
We camped under the stars all night.
It was a cold night, so we lit the fire.

easy.def: The time when it gets dark.
examples: We came home at nightfall.
Owls hunt at nightfall.
By nightfall, we were tired.

more.def: The time of day when it starts to get dark.
examples: We reached the campsite just before nightfall.
Bats come out to hunt at nightfall.
By nightfall the storm had passed.

easy.def: A long, loose shirt you wear to bed.
examples: She wore a nightgown.
My nightgown is soft.
Put on your nightgown.

more.def: A long, loose piece of clothing that you wear in bed, usually like a dress.
examples: She put on a soft flannel nightgown and climbed into bed.
My nightgown has small stars on it.
Grandma wore a long cotton nightgown.

easy.def: A loose dress to sleep in.
examples: She wore a nightie.
The nightie is pink.
A nightie is soft.

more.def: A loose, light dress that girls and women wear to bed.
examples: She put on her pink nightie.
The nightie was soft and long.
Grandma wore a flannel nightie.

easy.def: Happening every night.
examples: We have a nightly story.
The nightly news is on.
Her nightly walk is short.

more.def: Happening or done every night.
examples: Our nightly story time is my favorite part of the day.
The family watches the nightly news at six.
The moth made a nightly visit to the porch light.

easy.def: Every night.
examples: The owl hoots nightly.
We read nightly.
He brushes his teeth nightly.

more.def: Every night.
examples: The lighthouse shines nightly to guide ships.
Frogs sing nightly beside the pond.
She writes in her diary nightly.

easy.def: A scary dream.
examples: I had a nightmare.
The nightmare woke me.
A nightmare is a bad dream.

more.def: A frightening dream that happens while you sleep.
examples: I woke up from a nightmare.
The nightmare was about a giant spider.
Dad hugged me after my nightmare.

related.def: Very scary, like a bad dream.

easy.def: A small table beside a bed.
examples: The lamp is on the nightstand.
My nightstand has a book.
A nightstand is by the bed.

more.def: A small table that stands beside a bed.
examples: The lamp sits on my nightstand.
She put her glasses on the nightstand.
A glass of water was on the nightstand.

easy.def: The time when it is dark outside.
examples: Owls hunt at nighttime.
The nighttime sky.
I sleep at nighttime.

more.def: The time of day when it is dark and most people are asleep.
examples: Owls hunt in the nighttime when most animals are sleeping.
The nighttime sky was full of stars.
We went camping and heard strange noises in the nighttime.

easy.def: The number after eight.
examples: I have nine crayons.
My cat is nine.
There are nine kids.

more.def: The number 9, which comes after eight and before ten.
examples: A baseball team has nine players on the field.
School starts at nine o'clock.
She turned nine last week.

easy.def: One more than eighteen.
examples: I have nineteen coins.
Nineteen kids came to the party.
He is nineteen.

more.def: The number 19, which comes after eighteen and before twenty.
examples: The nineteen students lined up for the bus.
Nineteen days passed before the seeds sprouted.
She counted nineteen boats on the bay.

easy.def: Number nineteen in order.
examples: I am nineteenth in line.
The nineteenth page is torn.
He was the nineteenth to arrive.

more.def: Coming after eighteen others and before the twentieth.
examples: I was the nineteenth person to finish the race.
My birthday is on the nineteenth of June.
The nineteenth chapter of the book was the best.

easy.def: The number that comes after eighty-nine; nine tens.
examples: I have ninety stickers.
Ninety is a big number.
She is ninety years old.

more.def: The number 90, which comes after eighty-nine and is equal to nine tens.
examples: I counted ninety stickers in my book.
My great-grandmother is ninety years old.
The bus has room for ninety people.

easy.def: A trained fighter in old Japan who moved quietly and in secret.
examples: A ninja is in the story.
The ninja was quiet.
He dressed as a ninja.

more.def: In old Japan, a person trained in the art of moving quietly and in secret; also a character in stories and games.
examples: A ninja is in the cartoon.
The ninja moved without a sound.
He dressed as a ninja for Halloween.

easy.def: Number nine in a line.
examples: I am ninth in line.
The ninth day is cold.
She finished ninth.

more.def: Coming after the eighth one and before the tenth one.
examples: He finished ninth in the race.
My cousin is in ninth grade.
The ninth chapter ends with a surprise.

easy.def: To pinch or bite something lightly.
examples: The puppy nips my fingers.
A crab nipped my toe.
The goose nipped at us.

more.def: To give a small, quick pinch or bite.
examples: The puppy nipped my finger while we played.
A crab nipped at her toe in the shallow water.
The cold wind nipped at our noses as we walked to school.

easy.def: A small, quick bite or pinch.
examples: The dog gave a nip.
I felt a nip on my arm.
The nip did not hurt.

more.def: A small, quick bite, pinch or sharp feeling.
examples: The puppy gave me a playful nip on the hand.
There was a nip in the air on the autumn morning.
A nip from the goose made him jump back.

easy.def: A little cold.
examples: It is nippy today.
The nippy wind blew.
I saw a nippy morning.

more.def: A bit cold, in a way that nips at your skin.
examples: It was a nippy morning, so I wore a scarf.
The nippy air turned our noses red.
We walked home in the nippy wind.

easy.def: A gas that makes up most of the air.
examples: Air has nitrogen.
Nitrogen is a gas.
Plants need nitrogen.

more.def: A gas with no color or smell that makes up most of the air around us.
examples: Most of the air we breathe is nitrogen.
Plants need nitrogen to grow well.
Farmers add nitrogen to the soil to help crops.
